conviction_note: The reported quarter is pre-determined: the guide implies Q4 adjusted EPS of $2.66 +/-0.10 and consensus is $2.68-2.70. So the print turns on the first FY2027 guide against a $12.24 consensus that has risen 5% in 90 days on a base inflated by a $0.70 non-recurring tariff refund. This name's last two initial guides moved it -2.4% (guide 0.7% under consensus) and +8.2% (3.7% over). Peers TDG (guide under consensus, -4% premarket) and WWD (+7% EPS guide, margins moderating) lean negative. The Lockheed PAC-3 multi-year and the company's own 9% growth target lean positive. Net is close to balanced, so p_up is 48 on an abs move of 7.5 (scaled -0.3), and the findings sum to -0.3; the two measurements agree.
bar: Reported quarter: company FY2026 guide of adjusted EPS $11.65 +/-0.10 less nine-month $8.99 implies Q4 $2.66 (range $2.56-2.76) and ~$1.13B sales ($4.4B less $3.269B) (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/MOG/moog-inc-achieves-record-third-quarter-2026-results-through-szqtngplu3fc.html). Consensus Q4 EPS $2.68 on $1.12B (Yahoo, 5 analysts, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MOG-A/analysis) and $2.70 on $1.12B (Earnings Whispers, https://finviz.com/news/422860/moogs-fiscal-2027-outlook-must-prove-its-raises-arent-built-on-one-time-gains) agree with each other and with the guide. The bar that matters, FY2027: Yahoo consensus EPS $12.24 (4 analysts, range $11.64-12.81, up from $11.66 90 days ago) and sales $4.73B (+7.3%). That is ONE dated source; undated aggregators show $11.93-12.01, so the FY2027 bar is partly unsourced and every guidance finding is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is Q4 revenue against $1.12B.
positioning_check: Short interest 907,718 shares, 3.16% of float, 3.28 days to cover, up from 677,123 the month before (stockanalysis.com statistics, page updated 2026-11-19, settlement date not stated; https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mog.a/statistics/). Earlier FINRA via Curved Trading search snippet: 813.6K short, 3.0 DTC at the 2026-07-15 settlement. Not a crowded short. Skew is -3.58 vol points (upside paid), but the chain is very thin: 515 total open interest, ATM spread 24% of mid, and the event-implied move nets to 0 against 57.4% realised vol, so the option market makes no usable statement. Put/call OI 0.54. Stock at $334.19 is down 16% since the last print, 25% off its 52-week high and 2.2% down over 20 days. Forward P/E is about 28.7x against 43.6x trailing at the July print. Earnings Whispers bullish-sentiment reading is 67.8%.

findings.finding: The FY2026 adjusted EPS guide of $11.65 includes about $0.70 from a $30M IEEPA tariff recovery booked in Q3 cost of sales, which leaves an underlying base near $10.95. FY2027 consensus of $12.24 (Yahoo, 4 analysts, up from $11.66 90 days ago) therefore needs an initial guide of about +12% on the underlying base, or +5% on the reported base. Moog's last initial guide was $10.00 against FY2025's $8.69 (+15%) and sat 3.7% above the $9.64 consensus; whether management grows off the refund-inclusive or refund-exclusive base decides the sign.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Initial FY guide is the line: FY2025 guide of $8.20 against $8.26 consensus (Nov 2024) traded -2.4% premarket (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/moog-expects-2025-result-improve-below-estimates); FY2026 guide of $10.00 against $9.64 consensus traded +8.16% close to close on 2025-11-21 (baseline; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/moog-inc-sets-record-q4-sales-issues-2026-guidance/). In July 2026 a guide raise built partly on the refund was sold -7.0% (https://www.webull.com/news/15330621674038272).
findings.why_not_priced: The FY2027 consensus has been revised up into the print (11.66 -> 11.80 -> 12.00 -> 12.24 over 90/60/30/7 days on Yahoo), while the July refund-inclusive raise was sold. If the market had settled the base question, the estimate and the price would not be pulling in opposite directions: estimates are up 5% and the stock is down 16% since July.
findings.independence: Refund amount and treatment from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000067887/000162828026051294/mog-20260627.htm). Estimate trend from https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MOG-A/analysis. The Earnings Whispers preview frames the same question (https://finviz.com/news/422860/moogs-fiscal-2027-outlook-must-prove-its-raises-arent-built-on-one-time-gains). All three describe one arithmetic, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: Two direct aerospace peers issued FY2027 guides after Moog last spoke, and both decelerate. TransDigm (2026-11-10) guided FY27 adjusted EPS to a $47.52 midpoint against $48.4-48.7 consensus, with slowing growth in commercial OEM, aftermarket and defense and softer RPKs on oil and the Middle East, and fell about 4% premarket. Woodward (2026-11-18) guided FY27 adjusted EPS to $10.20-10.70, +7% at the midpoint on FY26's $9.78, with price realization normalizing to about 4% and margin expansion moderating on capacity spend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Moog-specific history for peer read-through. Moog's own initial guides moved it -2.4% and +8.2% (finding 1). Woodward's reaction on 2026-11-19 was not found.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: MOG.A is -2.5% over 5 days, which spans both peer prints. But Moog's own FY27 consensus went UP over the same 30 days (12.00 -> 12.24), so sell-side numbers have not absorbed the peers' conservative-initial-guide pattern. If they had, the FY27 estimate would have flattened or been cut.
findings.independence: Two separate documents: the TDG reaction report above and Woodward's 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108312/000117184326007561/exh_991.htm, 2026-11-18). These are proxies: neither company is a Moog customer, and the overlap is commercial and defense aerospace demand and pricing normalization. Moog also has Space & Defense, missiles and industrial/data-center exposure that these peers lack.

findings.finding: Lockheed Martin booked a $52.5B multi-year PAC-3 MSE production award in its Q3 2026 (MFC backlog $142.5B, about triple year-end 2025) and then placed large supply-chain follow-ons (L3Harris $4.7B propulsion, Boeing $14.7B seekers). Moog is the PAC-3 MSE steering-actuator supplier: its January 2025 award was over $100M, one of the largest in its Defense Division's history. The preview notes Lockheed's seven-year framework had not yet appeared in Moog's backlog at Q3, when Moog's 12-month backlog growth had slowed to 23% from 33%. A Q4 (quarter ended about 2026-10-03) or FY27-guide step-up in missile backlog is therefore plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog was a watch item when it slowed: the July print (backlog growth 33% -> 23%) was sold -7.0%, though reports attributed that mainly to earnings quality. No prior Moog reaction to a missile backlog step was found.
findings.why_not_priced: Lockheed's print is public, but no Moog sub-award has been announced since the 2025 contract, and the preview explicitly says the framework is not in Moog's backlog. If the market expected the flow-down, FY27 sales consensus would sit nearer the company's 9% growth target than at +7.3%.
findings.independence: Moog's supplier role is from Moog's own release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250129830001/en, 2025-01-29). The 'not yet in backlog' point is from the Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/422860/moogs-fiscal-2027-outlook-must-prove-its-raises-arent-built-on-one-time-gains). Netted for scale: missiles are about $275M of $4.4B sales (about 6%), so this is a backlog and sentiment item, not a FY27 EPS mover by itself.

findings.finding: The reported quarter sits inside the company's own guide. FY guide $11.65 +/-0.10 less nine-month $8.99 implies Q4 adjusted EPS of $2.66 ($2.56-2.76), and consensus is $2.68 (Yahoo) and $2.70 (EW). Implied Q4 sales of about $1.13B sit against $1.12B consensus. Moog has beaten EPS consensus four straight quarters, by 15%, 19%, 12% and 40%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 40% Q3 beat was sold -7.0% on 2026-07-31. The Q1 and Q2 beats with raises bought +6.0% and +2.3% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus sits on the guide midpoint. The only unpriced part is Moog's habit of clearing its own guide, which this name has not consistently paid for.
findings.independence: The guide arithmetic rests on the same Q3 release as finding 1 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/MOG/moog-inc-achieves-record-third-quarter-2026-results-through-szqtngplu3fc.html), but this finding uses it for the quarter rather than the forward base. The consensus agrees across Yahoo and the Earnings Whispers preview.

findings.finding: The Q3 10-Q shows $30M of IEEPA tariff recovery recognized, $10M received in cash and $20M held in prepaid and other current assets, with recovery judged 'probable' after the 2026-02-20 Supreme Court ruling. No figure for further claims is disclosed, so Q4 could carry more refund benefit or none.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 refund-aided beat was sold -7.0%, and reports cited 'one-off gains cloud profit strength' (https://www.webull.com/news/15330621674038272).
findings.why_not_priced: Any further refund will be stripped by the market, as it was in July. It matters only through the FY27 base question in finding 1, so on its own it is worth about zero.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1's refund amount. It is kept separate because it bears on Q4 quality, not on the FY27 base.

findings.finding: At the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference on 2026-09-10, inside the quarter, management projected a 9% revenue CAGR over three years and said backlog growth outpaced 15% revenue growth (total backlog $7.1B). FY2027 sales consensus is $4.73B (+7.3% on $4.41B). A FY27 sales guide near the 9% target (about $4.8B) would sit above consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY2026 sales guide of $4.2B against $4.01B consensus came with a +8.16% reaction (baseline; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/moog-inc-sets-record-q4-sales-issues-2026-guidance/).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY27 sales growth (+7.3%, low $4.60B) sits below the company's own stated medium-term rate. If analysts had anchored on it, the mean would be near $4.8B. The source is an AI summary of a fireside chat, and a 3-year CAGR is not a FY27 guide, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy for the guide from an AI-generated event summary (snippet quality), not a primary document. Consensus from https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MOG-A/analysis.

findings.finding: Boeing delivered 161 commercial jets in Q3 2026, 22 of them 787s (62 year to date). Leeham reports North Charleston holding at 8 widebodies a month, constrained by engines and seats, and 737 MAX wing supply pacing the ramp. Moog's Commercial Aircraft segment ($254M in Q3, +17%) is heavily tied to 787 flight controls.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Moog-specific reaction found for OEM-rate news. In July, management said commercial production was 'steadily increasing as bottlenecks are addressed'.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as public OEM data. It bears only on how much commercial OEM growth Moog puts in a FY27 guide; a flat 787 rate caps that.
findings.independence: Boeing's own Q3 delivery release (https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2026/Boeing-Announces-Third-Quarter-Deliveries/default.aspx). This is a proxy. Commercial Aircraft is about 23% of Moog sales, and the rest (defense, space, industrial) is growing double digits, so it is sized net and small.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the stock is down 16% since the July print and 25% off its high, the forward P/E has compressed to about 28.7x from a 43.6x trailing multiple in July, the 25-delta skew is -3.6 vol points (upside paid, thin chain) and short interest is a modest 3.2% of float. The July de-rating has already absorbed much of the earnings-quality concern.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the prior de-rating in 2025 (the Jan 2025 print -7.2%), subsequent prints were -0.2%, -1.8% and then +8.2% on the guide (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the market's own state and largely is the price. It is filed small because skew and de-rating lean the same way as the bullish sentiment reading, which would make an in-line guide less punishing than July.
findings.independence: The July multiple is from https://www.webull.com/news/15330621674038272. Skew and drawdown are from the sealed baseline.

baseline_tension: There is little to cut against: the run-up is flat to slightly negative (-2.2% over 20 days, -2.5% over 5), the skew mildly favours upside on an unusable chain, and the findings net to roughly zero, so nothing here fights the baseline.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): PAC-3 backlog finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5, because missiles are about 6% of sales.
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; the July beat was sold): Q4-inside-guide finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): remaining tariff-refund receivable finding cut from +0.1 to 0.0, since its only path to the stock is the FY27 base question already in finding 1.
Rule 6 (bar with one dated source): FY27 consensus has only one dated source, so the 9% CAGR guide-proxy finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.4; the other guidance findings were already small.
Rules 5 and 7 left standing: peer read-through and Boeing were already filed small as proxies; short interest was checked (3.2% of float, not crowded) before the negatives.
abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged at 7.5 and 48.
